newsitem.title: UK: Lasmo sees oil price barely changed.
newsitem.headline: Lasmo sees oil price barely changed.

text.p: Oil exploration and production company Lasmo Plc said it did not expect much short term change in the current crude oil price.
If anything there could be some price weakness, chief executive Joe Darby told Reuters.
Any short term weakness would be due to any Iraqi exports and increased production as oil fields come back to full capacity following the traditional summer maintenance period, Darby said.
"We don't see much upside. If anything we see some short-term weakness," he said.
Looking further ahead, Lasmo, which earlier reported net first-half profit rose to 26 million stg from 24 million, is conservatively planning on a 1998 oil price of $17.50 per barrel, Darby said.

First-half profit was helped by a mildly higher oil price. It averaged $19.40 per barrel compared with $17.82 a year earlier. But due to the pound's strength, the dollar increase translated in a mere two percent rise in sterling terms, Darby said.
Taxes fell in the first half due to lower production in Indonesia, but this positive tax impact was largely offset by higher finance charges.

The exploration and appraisal write off was unchanged at 18 million stg. Lasmo spent more in the first half on exploration and appraisal than a year earlier. But the write off remained the same due to exploration successes, Darby said.
"About 75 percent of our exploration and appraisal wells have been successes," said Darby.
He predicted taxes would remain broadly unchanged in the second half of 1997.

But the finance charge will likely show a slight rise in the second half, he added. The rise would be the consequence of the North Sea MacCulloch coming onstream. This could happen any day now, Darby said.
He expects the field's production to rise to about 50,000 barrels per day shortly after start-up.
MacCulloch, in which Lasmo has a 40 percent interest, was originally expected to come onstream in January. But mechanical problems and extra time needed to hook up facilities led to a delay.
This was the main reason for Lasmo's flat production of 171,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the first half of 1997.

Darby said the first-half had nonetheless been successful, pointing to four discoveries in Algeria, a significant gas discovery in Pakistan and the $453 million oil contract in Venezuela, which was won last month.
"Things look quite good from an operational point of view," he said.
